title: gallery
text:
The gallery demos live in rupaka/demos/ as JSON. They show what a good demo looks like, and the agent gives two of them to the model as examples. The data of the Sanskrit and jyotiṣa demos comes from the vedicreader and ganapati sources, not from memory:
import json
from rupaka.spec import *
from rupaka.spec import _gates
from rupaka.render import show, save, page
from rupaka.check import check, can_check, browser, in_thread

title: gallery
text:
The demos
Each demo has a gate. Here are the gate questions and the blocks of each demo.

g = gallery()
for k, s in g.items(): print(f"{k:24} {[b['type'] for b in s['blocks']]}\n{'':24} {next(_gates(s['blocks']))['prompt']}")

title: gallery
text:
Each demo is valid
validate finds no errors in any gallery demo.

test_eq({k: list(validate(s)) for k, s in g.items()}, {k: [] for k in g})

title: gallery
text:
The builder form
A notebook author can write the sandhi demo with the builders. The result is the same dict as the JSON file.

V = ['a', 'ā', 'i', 'ī', 'u', 'ū', 'ṛ', 'e', 'ai', 'o', 'au']
sd = g['vowel-sandhi']
d = demo('vowel-sandhi', 'Vowel sandhi', ask=sd['ask'], state=dict(a='a', b='i'), derive=[rules('sandhi', ['a', 'b'], 'join')],
         blocks=[row(wheel('a', V, 'End of word 1'), wheel('b', V, 'Start of word 2')),
                 gate('join', 'What do the two vowels become?', from_('join.alts'), 'join.out', context='For {a} + {b}:',
                      why='Say why, in one line, before you lock in.', again=True),
                 readout('{a} + {b} → {join.out}', label='The join', after='join'),
                 caption(sd['blocks'][3]['text'], after='join')],
         tables=sd['tables'])
test_eq(d, sd)

title: gallery
text:
The data
At 47°, the point is in Rohiṇī, pāda 3, in Vṛṣabha. At 30°, the start of Vṛṣabha, it is in Kṛttikā, pāda 2.

nk = g['nakshatra-pada']
test_eq(run(nk)['where'], 'Rohiṇī, pāda 3')
test_eq(run(nk)['rasi']['name'], 'Vṛṣabha')
test_eq(run(nk, dict(lon=30, show_pada=False))['where'], 'Kṛttikā, pāda 2')

For a + i, the join is e (guṇa). The wrong options come from the other rows of the table.

j = run(sd)['join']
test_eq((j['out'], j['name']), ('e', 'guṇa'))
test_eq(sorted(j['alts']), ['e', 'ā', 'ī', 'ū'])

With k = 60 the fused winner is B, which is in both lists. With k = 1 it is A, the top of one list.

rr = g['reciprocal-rank-fusion']
test_eq(run(rr)['fused'][0]['id'], 'B')
test_eq(run(rr, {**rr['state'], 'k': 1})['fused'][0]['id'], 'A')

title: gallery
gallery
text:
One page
save writes the whole gallery to one page that works from file://.

import tempfile
from pathlib import Path


p = save(list(g.values()), Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'gallery.html', title='rupaka gallery', lead='Predict first. Then the demo shows the rest.')
assert p.exists() and (p.parent/'fonts').exists()

In a notebook, show draws a demo:

show(g['reciprocal-rank-fusion'])

title: render
text:
One runtime draws a spec everywhere. A host element carries the spec as inert JSON, and the runtime mounts it:
The runtime boots on load and after each htmx swap. Nothing is templated into the script.

title: render
text:
The bundle
bundle joins the core, the fns, the blocks and the boot script in a fixed order. There is no bundler and no build step.


source

bundle
def bundle(
    kind:str='js'
)->str:
The runtime as one script (js) or one style sheet (css), with this package’s version in the script. three gives three.js.




source

assets
def assets()->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
The files of the runtime, in bundle order.


The script starts with the core and ends with the boot. Each block is in it.

js = bundle()
assert js.startswith('/* static/rupaka.js */') and js.rstrip().endswith('})();')
for n in manifests(): assert f"Rupaka.block('{n}'" in js, n
assert 'eval(' not in js and 'new Function' not in js and 'fetch(' not in js
assert f"version: '{__version__}'" in js and '{{version}}' not in js

Each block style uses only the --rk-* vars for colour, so a demo takes the look of the page that holds it.

import re


for p in assets().css[1:]:
    cols = re.findall(r'(?:#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,6}\b|rgba?\(|hsl\()', p.read_text())
    test_eq((p.name, cols), (p.name, []))

title: render
text:
three.js for scenes
A scene block draws in 3D with three.js. rupaka keeps a copy of three.js in rupaka/static/vendor/three/, so a scene works offline and loads nothing from a CDN.







item
value




version
three 0.185.0, from npm (three-0.185.0.tgz, integrity sha512-+yRrcRO2iZa8uzvNNl0d7cL4huhgKgBvVJ0njcTe8xFqZ6DMAFZdCKDP91SEAuj25bNAj7k1QQdf+srZywVK6w==)


files
three.core.min.js and three.module.min.js, as npm gives them, with no change


licence
MIT, in vendor/three/LICENSE


size
about 750 KB



0.185.0 is the last release that has the minified files. The tests check the hash of each file, so a changed file fails at once.
The hashes of the two files, as sha256:

for f, h in THREE.files.items(): test_eq(hashlib.sha256((VENDOR/'three'/f).read_bytes()).hexdigest(), h)
assert 'MIT License' in (VENDOR/'three'/'LICENSE').read_text()

The two files are ES modules: the second one imports the first. A module cannot load from file:// or from a sandboxed srcdoc frame, and those are places where rupaka draws. So three_js joins the two files into one classic script. It changes only the import and export statements: an import becomes a read from the first file’s names, and an export becomes a return. The script puts the names on window.RupakaTHREE, and it does nothing when it runs a second time.


source

three_js
def three_js()->str:
three.js as one classic script that sets window.RupakaTHREE, made from the two vendored module files.


The script has no module statement left, and it exports the names that a scene uses.

t = three_js()
assert not re.search(r'(^|[;}])\s*(import|export)\s*[{*]', t) and 'from"./three' not in t
for k in ('WebGLRenderer', 'MeshToonMaterial', 'ExtrudeGeometry', 'DepthTexture', 'REVISION'): assert f'{k}:' in t, k
test_eq(bundle('three'), t)

needs gives the vendored libraries that a list of specs needs. Only a spec with a scene block needs three.js.


source

needs
def needs(
    specs
)->set:
The vendored libraries that specs need: three when a spec has a scene block.



test_eq(needs(dict(blocks=[dict(type='readout', text='x')])), set())
test_eq(needs([dict(blocks=[]), dict(blocks=[dict(type='stack', blocks=[dict(type='scene', blocks=[])])])]), {'three'})

title: render
text:
The host element
host writes the element that carries a spec. JSON in a <script> must not hold </script>, so every < becomes \u003c. JSON.parse reads it back as <.


source

host
def host(
    spec
)->str:
The host element: a div that carries its spec as inert JSON.




source

spec_json
def spec_json(
    spec
)->str:
The spec as JSON that is safe inside a <script> element.



h = host(dict(id='x', ask='Do not stop at </script> here.'))
assert '</script>' not in h.split('<script type="application/json">')[1][:-len('</script></div>')]
test_eq(json.loads(h.split('json">')[1].split('</script>')[0]), dict(id='x', ask='Do not stop at </script> here.'))

title: render
text:
A static page
page writes one self-contained HTML file: the runtime, the style, the specs, and abhyasa’s palette. The fonts argument picks how the page gets its fonts:



fonts
what it does




'link'
links Literata and Libre Baskerville from ./fonts (save copies them)


'embed'
puts the fonts in the page as data URIs, about 160 KB more


'none'
uses the system serif; for a sandboxed srcdoc frame, which cannot load files





source

font_css
def font_css(
    fonts:str='link', base:str='fonts/'
)->str:
The @font-face rules: linked from base, embedded as data URIs, or none.


page takes one spec or a list of specs. A list makes a gallery page with a rule between the demos. When a spec has a scene, the page also holds three.js.


source

page
def page(
    specs, title:str=None, fonts:str='link', lead:str=''
)->str:
One self-contained HTML document that draws specs, with no network.


A page loads nothing from the network: no src, href or url() points at http. (The SVG namespace string is not a request.) With fonts='none' it has no @font-face rule.

spec = dict(rupaka=1, id='t', title='T', state=dict(a=1), blocks=[dict(type='readout', text='{a}')])
p = page(spec)
assert not re.search(r'''(src|href)=["']?https?:|url\(\s*["']?https?:''', p)
assert '@font-face' in p and '@font-face' not in page(spec, fonts='none')
assert 'data:font/woff2;base64,' in page(spec, fonts='embed')
assert 'window.RupakaTHREE=' not in p
s3 = page(dict(rupaka=1, id='s', state={}, blocks=[dict(type='scene', blocks=[])]), fonts='none')
assert 'window.RupakaTHREE=' in s3 and not re.search(r'''(src|href)=["']?https?:|url\(\s*["']?https?:''', s3)

save writes a page to a file. With linked fonts, it copies the font files beside it, so the file works from file://.


source

save
def save(
    specs, path, fonts:str='link', **kw
)->pathlib.Path:
Write page(specs) to path; with fonts='link', copy the fonts to fonts/ beside it.



import tempfile


out = save(spec, Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'t.html')
assert (out.parent/'fonts'/'literata-latin-wght-normal.woff2').exists()

title: render
text:
Notebooks: show
show(spec) returns an object that a notebook draws. It gives two mime types:

application/vnd.rupaka+json: the spec, for a frontend that knows rupaka (a later leela change).
text/html: the whole page with fonts='none'. leela, Jupyter and VS Code draw it in a sandboxed frame. This works in leela today.



source

show
def show(
    spec
)->__main__.Show:
Draw spec in a notebook output.




source

Show
def Show(
    spec
):
A demo for a notebook output: the rupaka mime and a full HTML page.



mb = show(spec)._repr_mimebundle_()
test_eq(mb[MIME], spec)
assert '<script' in mb['text/html'] and '@font-face' not in mb['text/html']

title: render
text:
Markdown: md
md(spec) writes a ```rupaka fence with readable JSON. A renderer that knows rupaka mounts it; others show the JSON as code. md(spec, frame=True) writes a ```{=html} fence that holds a sandboxed frame. leela draws this in a Markdown cell today, with no change to leela.


source

md
def md(
    spec, frame:bool=False, height:int=760
)->str:
A Markdown fence for spec: readable JSON, or a sandboxed frame.



assert md(spec).startswith('```rupaka\n{') and json.loads(md(spec)[10:-4]) == spec
f = md(spec, frame=True)
assert f.startswith('```{=html}\n<iframe') and '<script' not in f and '<script' in f

title: render
text:
FastHTML: Demo and Assets
Demo(spec) is the host element as an FT component. Assets(prefix) gives the Link and the Script for a server that serves the bundle at prefix. A server that shows scenes also serves bundle('three') as three.js at the same prefix. The runtime loads it from there the first time that a scene mounts, and only then.


source

Assets
def Assets(
    prefix:str='/rupaka', v:str=''
):
The style and the script of the runtime, served at prefix; v busts the cache.




source

Demo
def Demo(
    spec, **kw
):
The host element of spec for a FastHTML page.



x = to_xml(Demo(dict(id='d', ask='a </script> b')))
assert '<script type="application/json">' in x and 'data-rupaka' in x and 'a \\u003c/script> b' in x
test_eq(to_xml(Assets(v='1')[1]), '<script src="/rupaka/rupaka.js?v=1"></script>')

version() is a short hash of the bundle, for a cache-busting v.


source

version
def version()->str:
A short hash of the script and the style.



test_eq(len(version()), 10)

title: agent
text:
author(concept, ask) asks a model for one demo on a concept. The model writes data only: a JSON spec. It never writes code. Then the loop checks the spec, and gives the errors back to the model to fix:
ask(prompt, sp) is any function that returns text, as in abhyasa. The tests use a fake one.

title: agent
text:
The catalog
The prompt lists the blocks and fns from their manifests, so it never names a block that the runtime does not have.


source

catalog
def catalog()->str:
The blocks and fns, with their purpose and props, as text for the prompt.


The catalog names every block and every fn.

cat = catalog()
for n in [*manifests(), *fn_manifests()]: assert f'- {n}: ' in cat, n
print(cat[:600])

title: agent
text:
The system prompt
The system prompt gives the rules of a good demo, the shape of a spec, and the catalog.


source

demo_sp
def demo_sp()->str:
The system prompt of the demo agent.



assert 'You never write code' in demo_sp() and '- wheel: ' in demo_sp()

title: agent
text:
The user prompt
The user prompt describes the concept, the first error of the learner (if there is one), and two gallery demos as examples. near picks the gallery demos that share the most words with the concept. A long table in an example is cut to three rows.


source

near
def near(
    concept, k:int=2
)->list:
The k gallery demos that share the most words with concept.




source

demo_prompt
def demo_prompt(
    concept, first_error:str='', examples:tuple=()
)->str:
The prompt that asks for a demo on concept, a dict with name, statement, subject and misconceptions.



c = dict(name='Reciprocal rank fusion', statement='Sum 1/(k + rank) over the lists.', subject='ml', misconceptions=['raw scores add'])
p = demo_prompt(c, 'You add the raw scores.', near(c))
assert 'first error: You add the raw scores.' in p and '"id": "reciprocal-rank-fusion"' in p

title: agent
text:
The repair prompt
The repair prompt gives back the spec and only its errors.


source

repair_prompt
def repair_prompt(
    spec, errors
)->str:
The prompt that asks the model to fix only errors in spec.

title: agent
text:
Parse
parse_json finds the JSON object in a reply, also inside a fence or after some text.


source

parse_json
def parse_json(
    s:str
)->dict:
The first JSON object in s. Raise ValueError when there is none.



test_eq(parse_json('Here:\n```json\n{"a": 1}\n```'), {'a': 1})
test_fail(lambda: parse_json('no json'), contains='no JSON')

title: agent
text:
author
author runs the loop. It stamps the spec with the schema, an id and the concept slug. log, when given, gets one entry for each failed try.


source

author
def author(
    concept, ask, first_error:str='', examples:NoneType=None, check:bool=True, repairs:int=2, log:list=None
)->dict | None:
A checked demo spec on concept from the model ask, or None after repairs failed repairs.



Tests with a fake model
fake replies from a list, one reply for each call, and keeps the prompts.

from rupaka.spec import examples as block_examples


def fake(*replies):
    calls = []
    def ask(p, sp=''): calls.append(p); return replies[min(len(calls), len(replies)) - 1]
    ask.calls = calls
    return ask
good = json.dumps(block_examples()['gate'])

A good spec passes on the first call. The spec gets the concept slug.

a = fake(good)
s = author(dict(name='Sums', slug='sums'), a, check=False)
test_eq((s['concept'], len(a.calls)), ('sums', 1))

A spec with one error gets one repair. The repair prompt names the error.

broken = json.loads(good); del broken['blocks'][1]['after']
a, log = fake(json.dumps(broken), good), []
s = author('Sums', a, check=False, log=log)
assert s is not None and len(a.calls) == 2
assert 'gives away the answer of gate "sum"' in a.calls[1] and 'Fix only these errors' in a.calls[1]
test_eq(log[0]['tries'], 1)

Three bad replies give up quietly: the result is None, and the log has three entries.

log = []
test_eq(author('Sums', fake('not json', json.dumps(broken), '{}'), check=False, log=log), None)
test_eq(len(log), 3)

A model that fails gives up too, with no exception.

def down(p, sp=''): raise ConnectionError('no network')
test_eq(author('Sums', down, check=False), None)

With a browser, check runs too, and a good spec still passes in one call.

from rupaka.check import can_check


if can_check(): assert author('Sums', fake(good)) is not None

title: agent
text:
A live run
A live run uses a real model, so it is not part of the tests. With the rishi package and its model claude/sonnet, it looks like this:
from rishi import Chat, resp_text
def ask(p, sp=''):
    chat = Chat('claude/sonnet', sp=sp)
    try: return resp_text(chat(p))
    finally: chat.close()
log = []
spec = author(dict(name='Guṇa sandhi', statement='a or ā before i, u or ṛ gives e, o or ar.', subject='sanskrit'), ask, log=log)
The first live run (26 October 2026, claude/sonnet, three concepts: guṇa sandhi, cosine similarity and binary search):








concept
result
model calls




guṇa sandhi
passed on the first try
1


cosine similarity
passed after one repair: a point showed the answer before the gate, and the think rule caught it
2


binary search
passed on the first try
1



So 3 of 3 passed, 2 of them on the first try. One spec put {n} in its plain-text ask. The check could not see it, so validate now refuses a template in a plain-text prop.

title: rupaka
text:
rupaka (रूपक) means a form, a play that the audience sees, and the figure of speech that shows one thing through another. A rupaka demo is one interactive figure that teaches one idea. The learner changes the inputs and sees the result change.
A demo never shows the answer first. Each demo follows one loop:
The validator enforces step 1: a block that shows a value which the answer depends on must wait for the gate. An explainer is the one exception. It has "mode": "learn" and no gate, so it shows a thing at once (see Explainers below).

title: rupaka
text:
What a demo is
A demo is a JSON spec, not code. It has a small state, derived values from named functions (fns), and a list of blocks. A model can write a spec safely, because a spec cannot run code.



part
what it is




block
a reusable UI part in rupaka/blocks/<name>/: its JS, its CSS, a block.json manifest and an example


fn
a pure function that computes a derived value: rules, rrf, softmax, lookup, expr, field, ids, pick, sort, fmt


gate
the block that asks for the prediction and hides the result until the lock in


spec
the JSON object: state, derive, blocks and tables, and a mode that is predict (the default) or learn



The blocks are gate, readout, caption, row, stack, slider, toggle, choice, wheel, ranklist, bars, axis, point, plot, grid and pixels. For 3D, a scene holds body, force, label3d and shot blocks (see the section on 3D scenes below).

title: rupaka
text:
Install
pip install rupaka
The headless check needs playwright: pip install "rupaka[check]". It uses the Chromium that playwright install chromium gives, or the browser in $FASTCDP_CHROME. It never runs your everyday Chrome.

title: rupaka
text:
How to use
Build a spec with the builders, or write the JSON.

from rupaka.spec import *


d = demo('sum', 'A sum', ask='Predict the sum before you see it.', state=dict(a=2, b=3), derive=[expr('a + b', 'sum')],
         blocks=[gate('s', 'What is {a} + {b}?', [4, 5, 6], 'sum', why='Say why, in one line.'),
                 readout('{a} + {b} = {sum}', after='s')])

validate returns the errors. An empty list means the spec is good.

assert validate(d) == []

A readout that shows the sum before the gate breaks the think rule:

bad = {**d, 'blocks': [d['blocks'][0], readout('{a} + {b} = {sum}')]}
validate(bad)

Then put the demo where the learner is:







where
how




a notebook (leela, Jupyter)
show(spec): an HTML output in a sandboxed frame, and the application/vnd.rupaka+json mime


Markdown
md(spec) writes a ```rupaka fence; md(spec, frame=True) writes a frame that leela draws today


a FastHTML page
Demo(spec) and Assets('/rupaka'); serve bundle('js') and bundle('css') at that prefix


a file
save(spec, 'demo.html') writes one page that works from file:// with no network



check(spec) draws the demo in headless Chrome and plays it. author(concept, ask) asks a model for a demo, and checks and repairs it.

title: rupaka
text:
The host API
A host page can read and change a demo that it mounted. In these calls, el is the element that holds the demo: the [data-rupaka] element, or the element that you gave to Rupaka.mount.



call
what it does




Rupaka.state(el)
gives a copy of the input keys (the keys of spec.state) and their values


Rupaka.set(el, state)
sets the input keys that state has, then runs derive one time and draws one time. It ignores other keys.


Rupaka.options(el, gate)
gives the option values of the gate gate, in the order that the gate shows them. Each value is the value itself, not the text that the gate shows. The gate reads options from the state after derive, and this call does the same. An unknown gate gives null.


Rupaka.settle(el, gate, pick, {answer})
closes the gate gate as if the learner picked pick. It draws the verdict and shows the blocks that wait for the gate. With pick null, the gate closes with no verdict. An unknown gate does nothing and gives false. The options object is optional.


Rupaka.open(el, gate)
opens the closed gate gate again, as the Try another button of the gate does. It removes the pick, the reason and the verdict, and hides the blocks that wait for the gate. It draws one time. It does not move the focus. A gate that is open does not change, and the call gives true. A gate that waits for the host to save a prediction does not open, and the call gives false. An unknown gate does nothing and gives false.


Rupaka.mount(el, spec, {save})
calls save(state) after each change of an input key. state is the value that Rupaka.state(el) gives.



Rupaka.set, Rupaka.settle and Rupaka.open never send rk-predict, never add to st.log and never call save. Rupaka.options only reads. A lock does not stop Rupaka.set. Each call throws an error when no demo is mounted in el.
To show one demo in two windows, mount the spec in each window. Send Rupaka.state of the first copy to the second window, and call Rupaka.set there. To send a pick, send its index in Rupaka.options of the first copy. In the second window, find the value at that index in Rupaka.options, and call Rupaka.settle with it. When the learner in the first window clicks Try another, call Rupaka.open in the second window.
A host can remove the gate answers from the spec of a copy that a room sees, so that the room cannot read them early. Then give the answer to Rupaka.settle in answer. The gate uses it to draw the verdict. answer is {is: value} or a path in the state, as in a gate. When the spec has an answer, the gate uses the answer in the spec. Rupaka does not write answer into the spec or the state. When the spec has no answer and you give no answer, the gate closes with no verdict.
rupaka.poll makes a question for a room from a gate. of_gate(spec, gate) gives the question and the index of the answer. public(p) gives the part that the room sees.

title: rupaka
text:
3D scenes
A scene block draws a physical thing in 3D: a jet that hovers, a gearbox, a molecule. It holds four kinds of part:



block
what it is




body
a primitive (box, cylinder, cone, sphere, capsule, torus) or a group. in puts a body in another body, so a compound part moves as one. A state key in rot turns it


force
an arrow on a body. Its length is mag times the scene scale, so arrows compare. mag can be a state key or a derived key


label3d
a chip on a point, with a leader line. Chips never overlap: each chip goes to a free place around its point


shot
a named camera: wide, side, front, top or close:<body id>. The scene finds the framing from the bounds of what shows



The scene has a toon look: flat colours in three soft bands, ink outlines, a soft floor and a contact shadow. The colours come from the page theme, in light and dark. With bind, a scene builds one step at a time: a part with step: n shows from step n, and the camera moves to the newest shot. With prefers-reduced-motion, the camera cuts and parts show at once. The think rule holds: a force or a label that shows the answer of a gate must wait for the gate.
s = demo('lift', state=dict(step=1, cam='wide', w=4), derive=[expr('w * 2', 'up')],
         blocks=[gate('g', 'What is twice {w}?', [6, 8], 'up'),
                 scene(body('base', 'box', [2, 1, 2]), force([0, 1, 0], 'up', on='base', at=[0, 1.5, 0], label='lift, {up}', after='g'),
                       shot(bind='cam'), shot('close:base', step=2), bind='step', steps=['A box.', 'Look closer.'])])
rupaka keeps a copy of three.js (0.185.0, MIT) in rupaka/static/vendor/three/. It loads only for a spec that has a scene, and never from a CDN:

page, save, show and md(frame=True) put three.js in the page when a spec has a scene, so the page works offline and from file://.
A server that serves the runtime at a prefix also serves bundle('three') as three.js at that prefix, beside rupaka.js. The runtime loads it from there the first time that a scene mounts. A host that serves it at another place sets Rupaka.base before the first scene mounts.


Scenes and the board
The board of the screen guide speaks one line for each step. It drives a scene with the host API, so “again”, “slower” and “next” need no new code:



board operation
host call




{"op": "step", "n": 3} with a scene spec
Rupaka.set(el, {step: 3}), where step is the bind of the scene


{"op": "demo", "set": {...}}
Rupaka.set(el, {...}), for example a slider value or a step


{"op": "cam", "shot": "side"}
Rupaka.cam(el, 'side'). It sets the key that a shot block binds. It gives false for a bad name, or when the scene has no bound shot



shots(spec) gives the shot names that a spec knows, so a host can check a cam operation before it draws. Each scene element also tells its state: data-rk-shot is the shot now, and data-rk-still is 1 when nothing moves.


Explainers
Sometimes the learner must see a thing before there is a good question, for example how a jet hovers. An explainer shows a scene at once, with no prediction step. Set "mode": "learn" on the spec. Then validate lets the spec have no gate. All the other checks still run.

An explainer cannot have a gate, and no block can wait for a gate or lock to a gate. validate refuses each one and says what to remove.
With no mode, or with "mode": "predict", a spec with no gate is refused as before. A mode that is not predict or learn is refused.
The runtime shows a small “Explainer” label above the title, so the learner knows that there is no prediction step. The .rk element has data-rk-mode="learn".

ex = demo('box', 'A box', mode='learn', state=dict(step=1), blocks=[scene(body('b', 'box', [1, 1, 1]), bind='step', steps=['A box.'])])

title: rupaka
text:
The gallery
rupaka/demos/ holds hand-made demos: vowel sandhi, reciprocal rank fusion, softmax and temperature, nakṣatra and pāda, and a parabola.

title: rupaka
text:
Develop
The notebooks in nbs/ are the source of the Python. The JS and CSS are hand-written files under rupaka/static/, rupaka/blocks/ and rupaka/fns/.
uv sync
uv run nbdev-prepare
uv run pytest

title: poll
text:
A presenter can ask a room the question of a demo gate. of_gate makes a choice question from the gate, with no model call. public keeps the part of a question that the room sees.
abhyasa and Leela share this module. abhyasa had the same contract first, as abhyasa.talk.ask_from_gate and public_ask.

title: poll
text:
A path in the state
_at reads a path such as fused.0.id in the state. A path that is not in the state gives _NONE, so a value of None is not the same as no value. It reads own keys only, as the runtime does: __proto__, prototype and constructor give _NONE.
A path reads into lists, and a missing key gives _NONE:

st = dict(a=None, xs=[dict(id='p')], constructor=1)
assert _at(st, 'a') is None and _at(st, 'xs.0.id') == 'p'
assert _at(st, 'b') is _NONE and _at(st, 'xs.1') is _NONE and _at(st, 'constructor') is _NONE

title: poll
text:
A question from a gate
The options of a gate are a list, or {"from": path} in the state of the spec. The answer is {"is": value}, or a path in the state. of_gate reads the state of the spec and does not run derive. A path that needs derive gives None. Fewer than 2 or more than 6 options give None, and so does an answer that is not an option. The prompt gets the values of the state. A {name} with no value stays as it is.


source

of_gate
def of_gate(
    spec:dict, gate:str
)->dict | None:
A choice question from the gate gate of spec, with the index of the right option; None when the gate can not be a room question.


The gallery gates with fixed options and a fixed answer give a question. The gates that need derive give None, and so does an unknown gate.

g = gallery()
assert of_gate(g['parabola-vertex'], 'move') == dict(kind='choice', q='b goes from 0 to 2. Where does the lowest point move?',
                                                     options=['Left and down', 'Right and down', 'Straight up', 'It stays'], answer=0)
assert of_gate(g['reciprocal-rank-fusion'], 'win') is None   # the answer needs derive
assert of_gate(g['vowel-sandhi'], 'join') is None            # the options need derive
assert of_gate(g['softmax-temperature'], 'nope') is None

A gate in a row, with its options and its answer in the state:

spec = dict(state=dict(k=60, opts=['x', 'y'], best='y'), blocks=[dict(type='row', blocks=[dict(type='gate', id='g', prompt='With k = {k} and {m}?',
                                                                                         options={'from': 'opts'}, answer='best')])])
assert of_gate(spec, 'g') == dict(kind='choice', q='With k = 60 and {m}?', options=['x', 'y'], answer=1)

The prompt and the options show values as the demo shows them in the browser. 2.0 shows as 2, null shows as nothing, and a minus sign is a true minus:

spec = dict(state=dict(b=2.0, t=0.1, x=-1.5, z=-0.0, n=None, ok=True, p=1/3), blocks=[dict(type='gate', id='g', prompt='{b} {t} {x} {z} {n} {ok} {p} {p:2}',
                                                                                       options=[2.0, 0.1, 1.5, True], answer={'is': 2.0})])
test_eq(of_gate(spec, 'g'), dict(kind='choice', q='2 0.1 −1.5 0  true 0.3333 0.33', options=['2', '0.1', '1.5', 'true'], answer=0))

title: poll
text:
The part the room sees
public keeps the kind, the question, the options, and most (the most characters of a words answer). It drops the answer and the source.


source

public
def public(
    p:dict | None
)->dict | None:
The part of question p that the room sees: no answer and no source.


abhyasa adds src to a question from a gate. public drops it, and the answer:

a = dict(of_gate(g['softmax-temperature'], 'hot'), src=dict(demo='softmax-temperature', gate='hot'))
assert a == dict(kind='choice', q='T goes from 1 to 2. What happens to the share of Paris?',
                 options=['It rises', 'It falls', 'It stays the same'], answer=1, src=dict(demo='softmax-temperature', gate='hot'))
assert public(a) == dict(kind='choice', q='T goes from 1 to 2. What happens to the share of Paris?', options=['It rises', 'It falls', 'It stays the same'])
assert public(dict(kind='words', q='Say why.', most=80)) == dict(kind='words', q='Say why.', most=80)
assert public(None) is None

title: spec
text:
A demo is one JSON object: the spec. It lists blocks, a small state, derived values and data tables. This module reads the block and fn manifests, gives a builder for each block, and checks a spec with validate.
validate enforces the think rule: a block that shows a value which a gate’s answer depends on must wait for that gate. So the learner always predicts before the demo shows the result. An explainer ("mode": "learn") is the one spec with no gate: it shows a thing at once, with no prediction step.

title: spec
text:
Manifests
Each block is a folder in rupaka/blocks/, with a block.json manifest. Each fn has a manifest in rupaka/fns/. A manifest gives the purpose in one line, the props with their types, and the keys. The validator and the agent prompt read the manifests, so they never drift from the code.


source

fn_manifests
def fn_manifests()->dict:
The fn manifests, by name.




source

manifests
def manifests()->dict:
The block manifests, by name.


Each block folder has its code, its style, its manifest and one example.

test_eq(set(manifests()), {'axis', 'bars', 'body', 'caption', 'choice', 'force', 'gate', 'grid', 'label3d', 'pixels', 'plot', 'point', 'ranklist', 'readout', 'row',
                          'scene', 'shot', 'slider', 'stack', 'toggle', 'wheel'})
for n in manifests(): assert all((PKG/'blocks'/n/f).exists() for f in (f'{n}.js', f'{n}.css', 'example.json')), n

The fns are rules, rrf, softmax, lookup, expr, field, and four small helpers.

test_eq(set(fn_manifests()), {'expr', 'field', 'fmt', 'ids', 'lookup', 'pick', 'rrf', 'rules', 'softmax', 'sort'})

title: spec
spec
text:
The expr grammar
expr holds a formula in a tiny safe grammar: numbers, names, + - * / ^, parentheses and a few math functions. The runtime parses it in JavaScript. This is the same parser in Python, so validate can check a formula and run it. There is no eval in either one. A name must be a state key, a constant or one of the functions.
_safe turns a math error into the value JavaScript gives, so both sides agree: nan or an infinity.
parse_expr returns a function of a dict of values, and the set of names that the formula reads.


source

parse_expr
def parse_expr(
    src:str, # the formula
    fns:dict=None, # more functions by name, on top of `EXPR_FNS`
):
Parse a formula. Return (f, names): f(env) gives a number, and names are the values it reads.


2*x^2 - 1 at x = 3 is 17. The power binds before the minus sign, so -x^2 at x = 3 is −9.

f, ns = parse_expr('2*x^2 - 1')
test_eq(f(dict(x=3)), 17)
test_eq(ns, {'x'})
test_eq(parse_expr('-x^2')[0](dict(x=3)), -9)
test_eq(parse_expr('max(a, b) + floor(7/2)')[0](dict(a=1, b=4)), 7)

Names that reach into objects, calls of unknown functions, and a second statement are refused.

for bad in ('constructor', '__proto__', 'alert(1)', 'x;y', 'x.y', '2 +'): test_fail(lambda: parse_expr(bad)[0](dict(x=1, y=2)), contains='expr')

title: spec
text:
The fns in Python
Each fn has a Python twin with the same result. validate runs the derive list on the opening state with these twins, so it can check that each gate answer is one of the options. The browser tests compare the two sides.
First, two helpers that copy the runtime: get reads a path such as fused.0.id, and show_value writes a value as the runtime does.


source

fmt_text
def fmt_text(
    s, st
)->str:
Fill {path} and {path:2} from the state, as the runtime does.




source

show_value
def show_value(
    v, d:NoneType=None
)->str:
A value as the runtime shows it: numbers rounded as toFixed(d) (default 4) does, with a true minus sign.




source

js_str
def js_str(
    v
)->str:
String(v) in JavaScript, for the values a spec holds.




source

get
def get(
    o, path
):
Read a path such as fused.0.id in dicts and lists; own keys only, as the runtime does.



st = dict(fused=[dict(id='B', value=0.0328)], k=-60, xs=[1, 2])
test_eq(get(st, 'fused.0.id'), 'B')
test_eq(get(st, 'fused.0.__proto__'), None)
test_eq(fmt_text('{fused.0.id} {fused.0.value:2} {k} {xs}', st), 'B 0.03 −60 1, 2')

js_str gives the text of String(v) in JavaScript, and show_value rounds as toFixed does, so a tie such as 1.03125 goes up:

test_eq([js_str(v) for v in (2, 2.0, 0.1, 1.5, -0.0, 1e21, 1e-7, 0.00001, True, None, 'a', [1, None])],
        ['2', '2', '0.1', '1.5', '0', '1e+21', '1e-7', '0.00001', 'true', 'null', 'a', '1,'])
test_eq([show_value(v) for v in (2.0, -1.5, 1/3, 1.03125, None, True, [1, None])], ['2', '−1.5', '0.3333', '1.0313', '', 'true', '1, '])

Now the fns. rules orders its alts with the same small hash as the runtime, so both sides give the same options.
rrf, softmax and lookup follow the runtime line by line.
expr gives a number, or a series of points with over. field gives the rows of an n x n grid, with noise from a hash that gives the same bits as the runtime. The small helpers finish the set.


source

noise
def noise(
    seed:int, i, j
)->float:
The noise(i, j) of a field with seed: mean 0, variance 1, and the same bits as the runtime.


run gives the opening state of a demo: the state, then each derive in order. Each gate starts open.


source

run
def run(
    spec, state:dict=None
)->dict:
The state of spec after the derive list, from its opening state or from state.


The fused scores of the two spike lists at k = 60: B is first, because it is in both lists.

sp = dict(state=dict(bm25=list('ACEB'), vec=list('DFGB'), k=60), derive=[rrf(['bm25', 'vec'], 'k', 'fused')], blocks=[])
st = run(sp)
test_eq(st['fused'][0]['id'], 'B')
test_close(st['fused'][0]['value'], 1/64 + 1/64)
test_eq(run(sp, {**sp['state'], 'k': 1})['fused'][0]['id'], 'A')

softmax at a high temperature makes the shares more equal.

sp = dict(state=dict(z=[2, 1, 0]), derive=[softmax('z', 'p', t=1), softmax('z', 'q', t=2)], blocks=[])
st = run(sp)
test_close(st['p'][0]['value'], 0.6652, eps=1e-4)
assert st['q'][0]['value'] < st['p'][0]['value']

field runs a formula on each cell of an n x n grid. Row i and column j go from 0 to n − 1. This formula fades a ramp into noise as t goes from 0 to 1000:

DIFF = 'sqrt(1 - t/1000) * (i + j)/30 + sqrt(t/1000) * noise(i, j)'
def fld(f, t=500, seed=7, n=16): return run(dict(state=dict(t=t), derive=[field(f, 'img', n=n, seed=seed)]))['img']
img = fld(DIFF)
test_eq((len(img), len(img[0])), (16, 16))
[round(v, 3) for v in img[0][:4]]

The same seed gives the same field, and another seed gives another field. At t = 0 there is no noise, so each cell is (i + j) / 30.

test_eq(fld(DIFF), img)
assert fld(DIFF, seed=8) != img
test_eq(fld(DIFF, t=0)[3][4], 7/30)
fld(DIFF, t=0)[3][:4]

title: spec
text:
validate
validate(spec) returns a list of errors. Each error has a path and one sentence, for example blocks[3].bind: "fused" is not in state or derive. An empty list means the spec is good. It checks, in order:

The shape: the schema number, the top-level keys, the mode, and a list of blocks.
Each derive: the fn exists, its props have the right types, and it reads only keys that come before it.
Each block: the type exists, its props have the right types, the required props are there, and each bind names a key. Each after and each lock names a gate, and no gate waits for itself. A block above its gate can wait for it, for example a mark on a figure.
A demo has at least one gate, and an explainer has none (see below). Each gate: its answer resolves on the opening state and is one of its options. A gate whose answer a live control can change names its inputs with context.
The think rule (below).
Text: each sentence has at most 20 words.

First, the prop types. A scene adds four: vec3 ([x, y, z]), vec3key ([x, y, z], where an item can be a state key), nums (one to three sizes) and texts (lines of text). _reads gives the keys that a value of a type reads, so the think rule can follow them.
_props checks the props of one block or one derive entry against its manifest. A prop with min or max in its manifest must be in that range. A prop with of must be one of the values in that list. It returns the keys that the entry reads.
_walk visits every block with its path and its parent, in reading order.

The think rule
The answer of a gate has a root key: for fused.0.id, it is fused. A block must wait for the gate when it reads a key that gives the answer away:

the root key itself;
each derived key that the root is computed from (raw inputs are the question, so they stay visible);
each derived key that is computed from any of these.

A fixed answer ({"is": ...}) has no root key, so the gate names the keys that give it away in hides. A block waits for the gate when it, or a block that holds it, has after set to that gate, or to a gate that itself waits for it.


Text
ASD-STE100 asks for sentences of at most 20 words. This cheap check counts the words in each sentence of each text prop.


source

long_sentences
def long_sentences(
    s:str
)->list:
The sentences of s that have more than MAX_WORDS words.



test_eq(long_sentences('Short one. ' + 'word ' * 21 + 'end.'), ['word ' * 21 + 'end.'])



validate
Now validate puts the checks together.


source

validate
def validate(
    spec
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
The errors of spec, each as path: sentence. An empty list means the spec is good.


_check_blocks does the block checks, the gate checks and the think rule. An explainer has no gate, so the think rule has nothing to check. Its blocks cannot wait for a gate or lock to a gate, and the error says why. It gives each scene to _check_scene (below).
_check_gate checks one gate: its answer, its options, its context, and the think rule for its answer.


Scenes
A scene holds body, force, label3d and shot blocks. The manifests check each prop alone. _check_scene checks how the parts fit together:

Each body id is used one time. A body that is in another body names a body above it, so a body cannot hold itself.
A size has the right count of numbers for its kind.
A force or a label that is on a body names a body of the same scene.
A shot name is wide, side, front, top or close:<body id>. A shot that binds a key names a state key with a good shot name, so a host can set it.
A part with a step is in a scene with bind, and the step is in the range of the steps lines.
The step key is a state key with an int from 1. There are at most 8 steps, 40 bodies, 12 forces and 12 labels, and a chip has at most 60 characters.



source

shot_error
def shot_error(
    v, ids
)->str | None:
Why v is not a shot name for a scene with the body ids, or None.


shots gives the shot names that the scenes of a spec know. A host checks the cam operation of a board with it.


source

shots
def shots(
    spec
)->list:
The shot names that the scenes of spec know, for the board’s cam operation.




Tests for validate
A good demo has no errors.

good = demo('sum', 'Sum', state=dict(a=2, b=3), derive=[expr('a + b', 'sum')],
            blocks=[gate('s', 'What is {a} + {b}?', [4, 5, 6], 'sum'), readout('{a} + {b} = {sum}', after='s')])
test_eq(validate(good), [])

A readout of the sum before the gate fails the think rule, with the path of the readout.

bad = deepcopy(good); del bad['blocks'][1]['after']
test_eq(validate(bad), ['blocks[1]: this readout shows "sum", which gives away the answer of gate "s"; add "after": "s"'])

An unknown block, an unknown fn, an unknown prop and a missing prop each fail with a path.

def errs_of(**kw): return validate({**deepcopy(good), **kw})
test_eq(errs_of(blocks=[*good['blocks'], dict(type='dial')])[0][:23], 'blocks[2].type: "dial" ')
assert errs_of(derive=[dict(fn='sum', out='sum')])[0].startswith('derive[0].fn: "sum" is not a fn')
assert errs_of(blocks=[good['blocks'][0], {**good['blocks'][1], 'colour': 'red'}])[0].startswith('blocks[1].colour: is not a prop of readout')
assert 'blocks[1]: needs "text"' in validate({**good, 'blocks': [good['blocks'][0], dict(type='readout', after='s')]})[0]

A bind to a key that is not in the state fails. So does an after that names no gate.

assert 'blocks[2].bind: "k" is not in state or derive' in errs_of(blocks=[*good['blocks'], slider('k')])
test_eq(errs_of(blocks=[readout('{sum}', after='t'), good['blocks'][0]]), ['blocks[0].after: "t" is not a gate', 'blocks[0]: this readout shows "sum", which gives away the answer of gate "s"; add "after": "s"'])

A field needs an n from 1 to 64 and an int seed. A bad formula fails with its expr: error. The names i, j and noise need no state key.

fd = demo('fd', state=dict(t=500), derive=[field(DIFF, 'img', n=16, seed=7)],
          blocks=[gate('g', 'Which corner is largest?', ['top left', 'bottom right'], is_('bottom right'), hides=['img']), pixels('img', 'Grid at t = {t}', after='g')])
def field_errs(**kw): return validate({**fd, 'derive': [{**fd['derive'][0], **kw}]})
test_eq(validate(fd), [])
test_eq([field_errs(n=v) for v in (0, 65, '16')], [['derive[0].n: must be from 1 to 64'], ['derive[0].n: must be from 1 to 64'], ['derive[0].n: must be of type int']])
test_eq(field_errs(seed='7'), ['derive[0].seed: must be of type int'])
test_eq(field_errs(expr='i +* j'), ['derive[0].expr: expr: "i +* j" has an unexpected "*"'])
field_errs(expr='i +* j')

A gate answer must be one of its options. A demo needs a gate.

test_eq(errs_of(blocks=[gate('s', 'Sum?', [1, 2], 'sum')]), ['blocks[0].answer: the answer "5" is not one of the options [\'1\', \'2\']'])
test_eq(errs_of(blocks=[readout('{a}')]), ['blocks: needs at least one gate: the learner predicts first'])

A live control that changes the answer needs a context on the gate, so the verdict names its inputs.

live = errs_of(blocks=[slider('a', lock='s'), *good['blocks']])
test_eq(live, ['blocks[1].context: the slider at blocks[0] changes the answer, so name the inputs, for example "For {a}:"'])
ok = deepcopy(good); ok['blocks'] = [slider('a', lock='s'), {**good['blocks'][0], 'context': 'For {a} + {b}:'}, good['blocks'][1]]
test_eq(validate(ok), [])

The think rule follows derived keys both ways. Here twice is computed from the answer sum, so a readout of twice must wait too.

t = deepcopy(good); t['derive'].append(expr('2 * sum', 'twice')); t['blocks'].append(readout('{twice}'))
test_eq(validate(t), ['blocks[2]: this readout shows "twice", which gives away the answer of gate "s"; add "after": "s"'])

A block inside a stack that waits for the gate passes, because the stack waits.

t['blocks'][2] = stack(readout('{twice}'), after='s')
test_eq(validate(t), [])

A fixed answer names the keys that give it away in hides.

h = demo('h', state=dict(m=1), derive=[expr('m * x', 'line', over=dict(x=[-1, 1, 3]))],
         blocks=[gate('g', 'Steeper or flatter?', ['steeper', 'flatter'], is_('steeper'), hides=['line']),
                 axis([-1, 1], plot('line'), y=[-3, 3])])
test_eq(validate(h), ['blocks[1].blocks[0]: this plot shows "line", which gives away the answer of gate "g"; add "after": "g"'])

A plain-text prop, such as ask or a label, cannot hold {path}: the runtime would show the braces.

assert errs_of(ask='The list has {a} items.')[0].startswith('ask: is plain text')
assert errs_of(blocks=[*good['blocks'], readout('{a}', label='a is {a}')])[0].startswith('blocks[2].label: is plain text')

Each sentence has at most 20 words.

assert 'more than 20 words' in errs_of(ask=' '.join(['word'] * 25) + '.')[0]



Explainers
An explainer shows a thing at once, for example a 3D scene that builds one step at a time. It has no gate and no prediction step. Only "mode": "learn" makes a spec an explainer. The default mode is predict, and then a spec with no gate is still refused. All the other checks still run. The runtime shows a small “Explainer” label above the title.
A scene with no gate passes as an explainer:

ex = demo('box', 'A box', mode='learn', state=dict(step=1), blocks=[scene(body('b', 'box', [1, 1, 1]), bind='step', steps=['A box.'])])
test_eq(validate(ex), [])

With no mode, the same spec is refused with the usual message. A mode that is not predict or learn is refused.

test_eq(validate({k: v for k, v in ex.items() if k != 'mode'}), ['blocks: needs at least one gate: the learner predicts first'])
test_eq(validate({**ex, 'mode': 'learning'}), ['mode: "learning" is not a mode; use predict or learn'])
test_eq(validate({**good, 'mode': 'predict'}), [])

An explainer cannot have a gate, and its blocks cannot wait for a gate. The other checks still run, for example on a text that reads a missing key.

test_eq(validate({**good, 'mode': 'learn'}), ['blocks[0]: an explainer has no gate; remove the gate, or remove "mode": "learn"'])
test_eq(validate({**ex, 'blocks': [*ex['blocks'], readout('{a}', after='s')]}), ['blocks[1].text: "a" is not in state or derive', 'blocks[1].after: "s" is not a gate; an explainer has no gate, so remove "after"'])



Tests for scenes
A small scene: a box and a cone, a force on the box, a label, and a shot that a host can set. The force shows the answer, so it waits for the gate.

sc = demo('lift', 'Lift', state=dict(step=1, cam='wide', w=4), derive=[expr('w * 2', 'up')],
          blocks=[gate('g', 'What is twice {w}?', [6, 8], 'up'),
                  scene(body('base', 'box', [2, 1, 2]), body('top', 'cone', [0.6, 1], [0, 1, 0], inside='base'),
                        force([0, 1, 0], 'up', on='base', at=[0, 1.5, 0], label='lift, {up}', after='g'),
                        label3d('the base', on='base'), shot(bind='cam'), shot('close:top', step=2),
                        bind='step', steps=['A box with a cone.', 'Look at the cone.'])])
test_eq(validate(sc), [])
test_eq(shots(sc), ['wide', 'side', 'front', 'top', 'close:base', 'close:top'])

A helper puts one bad part in the scene, and gives the errors.

def scene_errs(i, **kw):
    s = deepcopy(sc); part = s['blocks'][1]['blocks'][i]
    for k, v in kw.items():
        if v is None: part.pop(k, None)
        else: part[k] = v
    return list(validate(s))

An unknown body kind, a force on a missing body, and a bad shot name are each refused with a clear sentence.

test_eq(scene_errs(0, kind='pyramid'), ['blocks[1].blocks[0].kind: "pyramid" is not one of: box, cylinder, cone, sphere, capsule, torus, group'])
test_eq(scene_errs(2, on='wing'), ['blocks[1].blocks[2].on: "wing" is not a body in this scene; use one of: base, top'])
test_eq(scene_errs(5, name='close:wing'), ['blocks[1].blocks[5].name: "wing" is not a body in this scene, so "close:wing" is not a shot'])
test_eq(scene_errs(5, name='zoom'), ['blocks[1].blocks[5].name: "zoom" is not a shot; use wide, side, front, top or close:<body id>'])

A bound shot must start with a good name. A body cannot be in a body below it, and a size needs the right count of numbers.

bad = deepcopy(sc); bad['state']['cam'] = 'far'
test_eq(validate(bad), ['blocks[1].blocks[4].bind: the opening value: "far" is not a shot; use wide, side, front, top or close:<body id>'])
test_eq(scene_errs(0, **{'in': 'top'}), ['blocks[1].blocks[0].in: "top" is not a body above this one in the scene'])
test_eq(scene_errs(1, size=[1, 2, 3]), ['blocks[1].blocks[1].size: a cone needs 2 numbers'])
assert 'must be [x, y, z]' in scene_errs(1, at=[0, 1])[0]

A part goes only in a scene. A part with a step needs the step key, and the step must be in the range of the lines.

test_eq(errs_of(blocks=[*good['blocks'], body('b', 'box')]), ['blocks[2]: a body must be inside a scene'])
test_eq(scene_errs(5, step=3), ['blocks[1].blocks[5].step: the scene has 2 steps'])
nb = deepcopy(sc); del nb['blocks'][1]['bind']
assert 'blocks[1].blocks[5].step: a step needs a scene with bind' in validate(nb)

The think rule holds in a scene too. The force shows up, the answer of the gate, so it must wait for the gate.

test_eq(scene_errs(2, after=None), ['blocks[1].blocks[2]: this force shows "up", which gives away the answer of gate "g"; add "after": "g"'])

title: check
text:
validate reads the spec. check runs it. It writes the static page, opens it in a headless browser with playwright, and plays the demo as a learner would. The browser is always headless, so no window opens and nothing takes the focus.
These checks run in light and in dark mode:

title: check
text:
The browser
The check never uses the Chrome that you use every day: a headless run of that app shares its crash reporter, its updater and its app registration, and many runs can crash it. It uses, in this order: a path that you give, the path in $FASTCDP_CHROME, or the Chromium that playwright install chromium gives. One process runs one browser at a time, and each browser closes in a finally block. A scene draws with WebGL. A machine with no GPU (as CI) draws WebGL with SwiftShader, and new Chromium versions need --enable-unsafe-swiftshader for that.

import os


if not os.getenv('FASTCDP_CHROME'): test_eq(browser_path(), None)
test_fail(lambda: browser_path('/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome'), contains='everyday Chrome')

text:
Contrast
This script runs in the page. For each element with its own text, it finds the colour behind the text: the backgrounds of the element and its parents, and for SVG text, a shape behind it in the same group (the dot of a picked wheel item, the cell of a grid). It mixes in opacity, then gives the WCAG ratio. Disabled controls and hidden text are skipped.

title: check
text:
The parts of the check
_state reads the state of the demo from the page. _parity compares each derived value with the Python twin of its fn.
_boxes checks that each visible block has a box, and that each block with after is hidden before its gate. Chrome’s checkVisibility() does not see display: none on an SVG element, so VIS also looks at the element and its parents.
_play plays each gate: it picks the first option with the key 1, and locks in with ⌘↩︎.
_keys sends keys to each control and checks that the state moves. A control at one end of its range gets the opposite key too.
